chunks: From him, from some of our companions, from 'Abbad ibn Sulayman, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from whoever narrated to him, from Idris ibn 'Abdillah al-Qummi, who said:

I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, teach me how the lease of a mill becomes valid, for the water with us sometimes flows and sometimes ceases.' He said to me, 'Make the bulk of the lease in the months in which the water does not cease, and make the remainder in the months in which the water ceases, even if it is one dirham.'
ai.seo_question: How is the lease of a water-dependent mill validated when the water supply is intermittent?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the fiqh of *Ijarah* (leasing) in the context of variable utility, specifically for a mill dependent on intermittent water sources. By allocating rent proportionally to the reliability of the water supply, the Imam establishes a practical mechanism to mitigate *Gharar* (uncertainty) and ensure fairness, a principle that extends to other lease agreements as seen in the subsequent narrations regarding inheritance and sale of leased property.
